correctness.rationale: The exact removal criterion is derived from neighborhood traces. For |T|≤4, only closed 4-neighborhoods and four-element symmetric differences at incident point–line pairs require checking; Fano geometry gives necessary and sufficient omission classifications for every size. Every ≥5 omission contains a forbidden smaller pattern, all admitted ≤3 omissions extend to an admitted four-set, and automorphism actions have exactly the two claimed orbits. Two separately built Fano incidence models independently check every one of 16,384 subsets: symbolic redundancy inequalities versus geometric classification in Python, and direct single-detector removal plus trace comparison in C++. Both produce the complete 98,224,91,14,1 counts and 98 inclusion-minimal ten-vertex codes; Python enumerates all 336 graph automorphisms.

value.rationale: One-offline-detector identification on the Heawood/Fano incidence graph is a natural fault-tolerant coding problem on a canonical sparse symmetric network. The exact missing-sensor geometry, complete enumerator, invariant distinction from seven-sensor ordinary codes, and two symmetry types of all minimal placements answer motivated configuration-level questions beyond the general published criterion; the finite exact result has independent interest without requiring a general projective-plane theorem.
